population.note: 37 = the 31 REFERENCES-NO-IMAGE rows (18 MH HSC 12 + 13 MH SB 11) plus the 6 DESCRIBED-IN-TEXT rows the probe buckets separately. Every one was read.

rows.why: The stem gives only theta = 37 degrees; the horizontal rod length H = 2.1 m and the vertical rod length V = 1.5 m that the solution uses to build the radius r = H + V sin37 = 3.0 m are printed only in the figure, so the frequency cannot be reached from the text.

The inlined description names the marked points (-6,-4), (-4,0) and the maximum (-1,4) so g(-4)=0 is recoverable, but it says only 'a local minimum near x = 3' and never gives that minimum's y-value, which is exactly what g(3) asks for.

Parts (i), (iv) and (v) turn on the five segments' LENGTHS, and the inlined description gives only directions and stacking order - it even calls e 'a short vector' where the printed answer makes e equal in magnitude to a and c, so the text actively contradicts the key.

Neither the semicircle's radius R nor the current I is named in the stem, and the fact that the two straight sections lie along the diameter (which is what makes their contributions zero at O) exists only in the figure.

The stem names only 'a cyclic process ABCA shown in V-T diagram (Fig (a))'; which leg is the straight V-proportional-to-T line, which is isochoric and which is isothermal is readable only off that diagram, and that is the whole content of the p-V transformation asked for.
The three orientations of v and B are supplied only by Figs (a), (b), (c) - the stem gives no axis for either vector in any of the three situations, so no cross product can be formed.
The five capacitor values (8, 4, 1, 4, 4 microfarad) and the series/parallel topology the solution reduces are entirely in the figure; the stem supplies only the target equivalent of 1 microfarad.

The appended prose gives only the field direction; L and s are defined by the chord and sagitta of the arc drawn in the figure, and the relation (R-s)^2 + L^2 = R^2 that the solution reads off 'the upper triangle in the figure' cannot be reconstructed from the text.
The stem gives the three charges but not the geometry: AB = 4.0 cm and BC = 3.0 cm, plus the right angle at B that makes AC = 5.0 cm, are printed only in Fig. a.

The stem says only 'the system of charges shown in the figure' - the four alternating +q/-q charges, the square side r and the two r*sqrt(2) diagonals that the six-term sum is built from are all figure-only.
Neither the charge magnitudes (the solution uses 2 x 10^-6 C at B) nor the hypotenuse length (BA = 5 cm, giving BP = 5/sqrt2 cm) appears in the stem; both are printed in Fig. a.
The transcriber inlined the whole route network in prose - two routes A-to-N, three N-to-B, one A-to-S, two S-to-B - which is every number the 2x3 + 1x2 = 8 count needs.

recallGapNotes.summary: A deliberate hunt for figure-bearing rows the probe cannot see turned up ZERO unanswerable ones in this lane, and one answerable one. Low recall here is NOT a hidden MISS population: the phrasings the rule is blind to are almost all attached-image rows or student-draws prompts.
recallGapNotes.method: Scanned all 9,219 image-less lane rows for (a) every figure-word the rule does not cover, (b) the phrasings taken from the 61 WITH-IMAGE rows the rule fails to name, (c) stems whose SOLUTION cites a figure while the stem is silent (78 rows), (d) short set-member fragments, (e) labelled-node stems carrying no numbers.

onlyRowFound.why: Opens 'Consider optically denser lenses P, Q, R and S drawn below' and carries a full [Figure: ...] block for the four lens cross-sections. Answerable, so not a defect - but 'drawn below' matches no alternative in FIGURE_REF, so this row never enters the probe's output at all and its DESCRIBED bucket loses it. The DESCRIBED count is a floor for the same reason the MISS count is.

phrasingsTheRuleCannotSee: PLURAL figure nouns: 'Express the following CIRCUITS in symbolic form', 'Identify the gas laws from the following DIAGRAMS', 'The following PICTURES show population of bands'. The singular-only revert (documented in figureRefs.ts as a CBSE measurement) costs 8 switching-circuit set members and several chemistry rows here - all of which DO carry images, so nothing is lost operationally, but it is a large part of why MH HSC 12 recall reads 54%.

The picture IS a chemical structure and is never called a figure: 'Write the IUPAC names of the following STRUCTURES', 'Identify A and B in the following REACTION', 'Identify the functional groups in the following MOLECULE', 'Find out the type of isomerism exhibited by the following PAIRS'. This is the single largest recall gap in MH SB 11 (25% recall) and is almost entirely chemistry. Widening the noun list to structure/molecule/compound/reaction/pair would add ~280 lane rows of which the overwhelming majority inline their formulae as LaTeX and need no image - a precision disaster. Do NOT widen on this axis for these two exams.
'drawn below' / 'shown alongside' - no noun and no 'as': the one row above.

Bare 'the circuit' / 'the diagram' with no adjective: 'At what value should the variable resistor Q be set in the circuit such that the bridge is balanced' (WITH image, unnamed). The rule's circuit alternative requires following|given|adjoining|above after the determiner, and this form has none. About one lane row, image-bearing.

'Fig. a' letter-form with no preposition: searched for explicitly, ZERO occurrences among image-less rows - the Balbharati letter form in this lane always arrives as 'in Fig. a' / 'as shown in the Fig. a', both of which the rule already catches.
